newsitem.title: USA: Imation profits almost double in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Imation profits almost double in first quarter.

text.p: Imation Corp., an imaging and information firm spun off recently by Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co., said Wednesday its quarterly profits almost doubled, boosted by software sales and growth in Asia and Latin America.
Profits soared to $12 million, or 30 cents a share, in the quarter from $6.1 million, or 14 cents a share, in the year-ago period.

Revenues fell to $547.7 million from $576.1 million, with about half of the drop reflecting a decision to exit certain underperforming businesses such as the sale of non-branded duplicator diskettes and some graphic arts supplies.
Imation said the dollar's strength reduced earnings by 17 cents per share, and revenues by about 3.5 percent.
The year-ago results includes a pretax restructuring charge of $10.4 million, or 15 cents a share after-tax.

"We are progressing towards our three-year financial goal of $150 million improvement in economic profit between 1996 and 1998," said Chief Executive Bill Monahan. "However, the recent strengthening of the dollar makes the achievement of revenue growth difficult this year."
Gross margins improved to 36.3 percent compared with 35.1 percent in the first quarter of last year, the company said.
Imation also said its board increased authorisation to repurchase common stock to 6 million shares. The company repurchased about 514,000 shares during the first quarter.
The Oakdale, Minn.-based company had about 9,700 employees in more than 60 countries as of March 31.
Imation's stock fell $1.25 to $23.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
